Fact.Name: (Writable) Is this Form 1099-MISC's box 3 an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend?
Fact.Description:
THE PER-ITEM CLASSIFICATION INTAKE: the filer's own record of whether this Form 1099-MISC's box 3 is an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend.
THE DOCUMENT DOES NOT IDENTIFY THE PAYMENT, so the filer must. Box 3 is the form's residual money box — "Enter other income of $600 or more required to be reported on Form 1099-MISC that is not reportable in one of the other boxes on the form" — and the recipient's own instruction for it says to "identify the payment", naming payments to the beneficiary of a deceased employee, prizes, awards, taxable damages and Indian gaming profits among the things it may be. Nothing printed on the form distinguishes an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend from any of those, so no payer test or box test can decide this and the determination is the filer's.
NO DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY, and the unanswered case is handled on ../isAlaskaPfd rather than here, so that this intake stays a faithful record of what the filer said.
the application owes the screen.

Fact.Name: Form is reporting Alaska PFD income
Fact.Description:
Whether the Form 1099-MISC is reporting Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend income.
This reads ../writableIsAlaskaPfd complete-safe.
THE UNANSWERED ARM IS THE MODULE'S LEGACY ASSUMPTION, CONFINED. When the filer has not answered the classification question, this resolves TRUE, exactly as the constant did. Two reasons, and neither is inertia. (1) NOTHING IS AT RISK IN DOLLARS: Schedule 1 line 8g and line 8z are both addends of the SAME line 9 total ("Total other income. Add lines 8a through 8z"), so an item on the wrong one of the two changes no total on the return; the residue is a disclosure defect, not a computation defect. (2) IT MUST RESOLVE COMPLETE ON EVERY INPUT STATE: /alaskaPfd1099s and /nonAlaskaPfd1099s are Filters over this predicate and /alaskaPfdIncome and /form1099MiscOtherIncome gate on IsComplete of those Filters, so a predicate that could go Incomplete would drop a real Alaska PFD to $0 rather than merely printing it on the wrong line. A Switch whose default arm is a literal cannot.
WHAT WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED FOR THAT ARM. /eligibleForApf (this file, residence state = ak) reads filers:/filerResidenceAndIncomeState, which is itself answerable-and-unanswered, so it would put Incompleteness inside the Filter predicate — the failure mode (2) names — and "a Permanent Fund Dividend is paid only to Alaska residents" is Alaska statute, which is not vendored (invariant #3). filers:/receivedAlaskaPfd is worse than unhelpful as a signal: it is answered FALSE on all three committed scenarios whose Form 1099-MISCs ARE Alaska PFDs (scenarios/upstream/apf-single-resident-no-dep.json, apf-single-resident-no-dep-withholding.json, mfj-44k-ak-pfd.json), so deriving from it would zero the very returns the module was built for.
THE UNANSWERED ARM NO LONGER FILES. ../isComplete requires ../writableIsAlaskaPfd, so an item that takes this legacy arm is an incomplete report and /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Miscs (or its secondary twin) blocks submission; a live filer is asked the question. The three committed upstream Alaska PFD scenarios (apf-single-resident-no-dep, apf-single-resident-no-dep-withholding, mfj-44k-ak-pfd) answer it yes for each of their Forms 1099-MISC, so they take the answered arm.
WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED. /form1099Miscs/*/isCommunityIncome carries a Not(../isAlaskaPfd) conjunct and was FALSE on every item this dictionary could hold; it now computes. /communityPropertyAllocatedOtherIncome was structurally $0 for the same reason; it now computes. Both were built to receive exactly this and neither needed an edit — see the records file, and see the report's note that this falsifies the reason column of the /form1099Miscs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ correct-refusal allowlist row.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 3 characterisation options
Fact.Description: The uses of box 3 "Other income" that are not an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend: the three the recipient instruction enumerates (a prize or award, trade or business income, or any other taxable payment such as a payment to the beneficiary of a deceased employee, taxable damages or Indian gaming profits, which stay on Schedule 1 line 8z with no further branch), and the payer-side use the Form 1099-MISC instructions name for box 3: compensation paid to an H-2A visa agricultural worker who did not give the payer a valid TIN, which is wages and goes on Form 1040 line 1h.

Fact.Name: (Writable) What kind of payment is this Form 1099-MISC box 3 amount?
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "What kind of payment is this?" Help text: You said this Form 1099-MISC box 3 amount is not an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend. The IRS recipient instruction for box 3 says to "identify the payment," and names a prize or award as one example and trade or business income as a separately-routed one ("If it is trade or business income, report this amount on Schedule C or F"); everything else it names (a payment to the beneficiary of a deceased employee, taxable damages, Indian gaming profits, or other taxable income) stays on Schedule 1 line 8z with no further question. Options, as they should be presented: "A prize or award" (prizeOrAward) — routes to Schedule 1 line 8i instead of 8z so it is not entered twice; "Trade or business income" (tradeOrBusiness) — self-employment income the recipient earned running a business, which belongs on Schedule C or Schedule F, not this line; "Pay for farm work on an H-2A visa" (h2aAgriculturalWorkerCompensation) — wages an agricultural employer reported in box 3 because the worker had not given it a valid SSN or ITIN (the employer then also withholds backup withholding in box 4); these are wages and go on Form 1040 line 1h, not line 8z; "Something else" (other) — the remaining box 3 uses, which stay on line 8z. Asked when: ../isAlaskaPfd is answered NO (../writableIsAlaskaPfd is Complete and false) — a PFD is never asked this question. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to "something else" through ../isPrizeOrAward and ../isTradeOrBusiness both resolving Complete false — keeps the amount on line 8z (counted once) rather than risking it vanish while a characterisation is pending; ../isComplete does not require this answer, so leaving it blank does not block submission. Validation: Enum (/form1099MiscBox3CharacterisationOptions), no default. What the answer feeds: "prizeOrAward" moves the amount from /form1099MiscOtherIncome (Schedule 1 line 8z) to /form1099MiscPrizesAndAwards, which income:/prizesAwardsIncome adds to Schedule 1 line 8i automatically. The application must NOT ask the filer to enter the same prize again on the income:/writablePrizesAwards screen: that screen is only for prizes not reported on an entered Form 1099-MISC, and a second entry would count the prize twice on line 8i; "tradeOrBusiness" takes the amount off line 8z and puts it under the Schedule C receipts floor (../tradeOrBusinessOtherIncome): the return's Schedule C line 1 must cover it, a return with no Schedule C is refused, and a filer who reports it on Schedule F (or whose form is wrong) answers ../writableScheduleCReceiptsReportedCorrectly yes. The application should tell the filer to include the amount in Schedule C line 1 (or Schedule F), not to enter it a second time anywhere else; "h2aAgriculturalWorkerCompensation" takes the amount off line 8z and adds it to the payee filer's Form 1040 line 1h (other earned income) through /primaryFilerForm1099MiscH2aCompensation or its secondary twin; "other" and unanswered both leave the amount on line 8z.

Fact.Name: Box 3 amount is a prize or award
Fact.Description: Whether the filer identified this Form 1099-MISC box 3 amount as a prize or award. Unanswered resolves FALSE (complete-safe): the conservative default that keeps the amount on Schedule 1 line 8z via ../../form1099MiscOtherIncome rather than dropping it while a characterisation is pending.

Fact.Name: Box 3 amount is trade or business income
Fact.Description: Whether the filer identified this Form 1099-MISC box 3 amount as trade or business income. Unanswered resolves FALSE (complete-safe), the same conservative default as ../isPrizeOrAward. TRUE TAKES THE AMOUNT OFF SCHEDULE 1 LINE 8z: /form1099MiscOtherIncomeItems excludes the item, and ../tradeOrBusinessOtherIncome carries the box 3 amount into ../scheduleCReportedReceipts, so the Schedule C line 1 reconciliation and /knockoutForm1099MiscScheduleCReceiptsWithoutScheduleC hold it on Schedule C (or, by the per-document attestation, on Schedule F). The Form 8958 line 8z allocation (../communityPropertyAllocatedOtherIncomeUnrounded) skips such an item, because the Schedule C carries its own community split, and a spouse's trade-or-business item on a return that is not joint stays refused (../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ).

Fact.Name: Box 3 amount is H-2A agricultural worker compensation
Fact.Description: Whether the filer identified this Form 1099-MISC box 3 amount as compensation paid to an H-2A visa agricultural worker. Unanswered resolves FALSE (complete-safe), the same conservative default as ../isPrizeOrAward: the amount stays on Schedule 1 line 8z until it is identified. TRUE takes the amount off line 8z (/form1099MiscOtherIncomeItems excludes the item) and onto Form 1040 line 1h through ../h2aAgriculturalWorkerCompensation.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-MISC's box 3 H-2A agricultural worker compensation (Form 1040 line 1h leg)
Fact.Description: The box 3 amount, cents kept, when the filer identified it as compensation paid to an H-2A visa agricultural worker (../isH2aAgriculturalWorkerCompensation); $0 otherwise. Such compensation is wages: compensation for services under IRC 61(a)(1) and earned income under IRC 32(c)(2)(A)(i). Form 1040 line 1a is the Form W-2 box 1 total and this amount is on no Form W-2, so it goes on line 1h, other earned income, the same route income:/primaryFilerForeignGovernmentWagesOnLine1h takes for wages no Form W-2 reports (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-53). It is not self-employment income and owes no Schedule SE, and H-2A compensation is exempt from social security and Medicare tax, so it owes no Form 8919 either. An Alaska Permanent Fund dividend never reaches this arm. FAILS CLOSED: an answered H-2A item with a blank box 3 leaves this Incomplete.

Fact.Description: The sum, cents kept and rounded once, of ../h2aAgriculturalWorkerCompensation over the primary filer's own Forms 1099-MISC. An addend of income:/primaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome (Form 1040 line 1h), so it reaches the primary filer's earned income. $0 when the collection is unanswered or empty.

Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerForm1099MiscH2aCompensation, summed over the secondary filer's own Forms 1099-MISC; an addend of income:/secondaryFilerOtherEarnedIncome.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Part of this box 3 amount that is damages for a physical injury or physical sickness
Fact.Description:
SCREEN. Question: "Does any of the box 3 amount on this Form 1099-MISC come from compensatory damages for a personal physical injury or physical sickness? If so, how much?" Help text: The payer is told not to report compensatory damages received on account of personal physical injuries or physical sickness, and they are not income to you; damages for emotional distress caused by a physical injury or sickness count as physical-injury damages too. Punitive damages, damages for a nonphysical injury, back pay and interest on an award are taxable and stay in. If the payer reported excluded damages in box 3 and will not correct the form, enter that part here and attach an explanation to your return. Asked when: the item is not an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend and its box 3 is not identified as a prize or award or as trade or business income; never required. Validation: Dollar, not above the box 3 amount. UNANSWERED: complete-safe $0 through ../box3PhysicalInjuryDamagesExcluded, so the whole box 3 stays on Schedule 1 line 8z; ../isComplete does not read it.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../box3PhysicalInjuryDamagesExcluded, which ../box3OtherIncomeForLine8z subtracts from box 3 before the amount reaches /form1099MiscOtherIncome (Schedule 1 line 8z) and the line 8z Form 8958 allocation. An answer above box 3 makes that item's line 8z amount Incomplete rather than negative.

Fact.Name: Box 3 physical-injury damages excluded from line 8z, complete-safe
Fact.Description: ../writableBox3PhysicalInjuryDamages floored at zero, on an item whose box 3 reaches Schedule 1 line 8z (not an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend, not a prize or award, not trade or business income); $0 when unanswered or on any other item, so a stray answer on a line 8g, line 8i or Schedule C item moves nothing.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-MISC's box 3 amount as it reaches Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description:
Box 3 less ../box3PhysicalInjuryDamagesExcluded, cents kept. It is what /form1099MiscOtherIncome sums over /form1099MiscOtherIncomeItems and what the line 8z Form 8958 allocation halves (../communityPropertyAllocatedOtherIncomeUnrounded). With no exclusion answered it equals box 3.
FAILS CLOSED: the Switch has no default arm, so an unanswered box 3, or an exclusion above box 3, leaves this Incomplete rather than a guessed or negative amount.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC federal tax withholdings
Fact.Description: Total federal income tax withheld (box 4) across all Form 1099-MISCs, a Form 1040 line 25b addend. The item fact /form1099Miscs/*/federalWithholding is a bare complete-safe passthrough of the writable with NO Round (form1099Misc.xml, immediately above), and this total is Round(Sigma of the raw per-item cents): cents survive into the sum and the total rounds once, exactly what i1040gi page 23 asks for. Line 25b is a whole-dollar printed entry line. /form1099DivFederalIncomeTaxWithheld uses the same shape on the same reasoning (its item fact is likewise unrounded).

Fact.Description:
The complement of /alaskaPfd1099s over the same collection. It is empty only when the filer says every Form 1099-MISC on the return is an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend, or has said nothing (the classification's legacy unanswered arm).
THE TWO FILTERS PARTITION THE COLLECTION. /alaskaPfd1099s and this one read the SAME complete-safe predicate, one straight and one negated, so every Form 1099-MISC is in exactly one of them and no box 3 dollar can be counted twice or dropped between the two printed lines.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 3 items that reach Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description: The non-Alaska-PFD Form 1099-MISCs (/nonAlaskaPfd1099s) minus the ones the filer identified as a prize or award (../isPrizeOrAward) — a prize-classified item is excluded HERE and picked up instead by /form1099MiscPrizeItems below, so its amount reaches Schedule 1 line 8i (income:/prizesAwardsIncome) and not also line 8z. A trade-or-business-classified item (../isTradeOrBusiness) is excluded too: the recipient instruction sends it to Schedule C or F, and /form1099Miscs/*/tradeOrBusinessOtherIncome carries its amount into the Schedule C receipts floor, so it is neither dropped nor counted on line 8z and Schedule C together. An item identified as H-2A agricultural worker compensation (../isH2aAgriculturalWorkerCompensation) is excluded as well: it is wages on Form 1040 line 1h (/primaryFilerForm1099MiscH2aCompensation and its twin).

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 3 items identified as a prize or award
Fact.Description: The complement of /form1099MiscOtherIncomeItems inside /nonAlaskaPfd1099s: the non-Alaska-PFD Form 1099-MISCs the filer DID identify as a prize or award (../isPrizeOrAward). The two Filters partition /nonAlaskaPfd1099s exactly, the same straight/negated-predicate shape /alaskaPfd1099s and /nonAlaskaPfd1099s already use, so no box 3 dollar can be counted on both Schedule 1 line 8z and line 8i, or dropped from both.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 3 amounts identified as a prize or award (Schedule 1 line 8i addend)
Fact.Description: Total box 3 amount across every Form 1099-MISC the filer identified as a prize or award, an addend of income:/prizesAwardsIncome (Schedule 1 line 8i). Built so the amount is counted automatically, exactly once, without relying on the filer to re-enter the same dollar figure a second time on the separate income:/writablePrizesAwards screen — that screen is scoped (see its own Description) to prizes NOT already reported on a Form 1099-MISC the filer entered. CENTS ARE KEPT: income:/prizesAwardsIncome adds this to the manual line 8i amount and rounds once, because the 1040 instructions say to "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total"; rounding this leg first would lose its cents before the add (100.40 + 200.40 printing 300, not 301). COMPLETE-SAFE $0: the Switch's first arm needs /form1099MiscPrizeItems Complete; the default arm is a hard $0, so a return with no prize-classified Form 1099-MISC contributes zero without reading a money box. THE FORM 8958 ADJUSTMENT: /communityPropertyPrizeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, a negative cents-bearing addend, takes off half of every community prize item on an allocation return (this filer's own and a spouse's item freed by ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ alike), the same shape /form1099MiscOtherIncome uses for line 8z, so line 8i carries this return's half and the line 8z allocation no longer halves a prize.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 3, box 8 and box 15 other income (Schedule 1 line 8z)
Fact.Description:
Total box 3 "Other income" across every Form 1099-MISC the filer did NOT classify as an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend or a prize or award (/form1099MiscOtherIncomeItems), as a Schedule 1 line 8z addend. Whole dollars: the per-form box 3 and the complete-safe box 8 and box 15 amounts are summed WITH CENTS and the total rounds once, the shape /alaskaPfdIncome and /form1099MiscFederalIncomeTaxWithheld already use in this module.
BOX 8 ROUTE. Every Form 1099-MISC box 8 substitute payment is added through the per-item ../substitutePaymentsForOtherIncome wrapper, including a document whose box 3 is an Alaska PFD or prize. This is the sole box 8 addend: hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome (printed line 8z) and income:/otherIncome (line 9) both read this fact, so the payment is entered once.
BOX 15 ROUTE. Section 409A nonqualified deferred compensation is added the same way, through ../nonqualifiedDeferredCompensationForOtherIncome, for every document and inside the same Round. Line 8t was measured and rejected as the destination (it is the W-2 box 11 employee line) and the composed line 8z argument, with the named trade-or-business residue, is in the block comment above that wrapper. The additional tax the same box carries is NOT here: it is Schedule 2 line 17h, and /form1099MiscSection409AAdditionalTaxFloor only bounds the filer's own entry there.
WHY LINE 8z. The recipient's own box 3 instruction sends the amount to "the "Other income" line of Schedule 1 (Form 1040)", and for TY2025 that line is 8z, printed "Other income. List type and amount:". The 1040 instructions' Line 8z paragraph is the same instrument read from the other side: "Other income. Use line 8z to report any taxable income not reported elsewhere on your return or other schedules." This fact is the FOURTH addend of hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome (the printed 8z amount box), so the printed box and line 9 foot from the same value by construction; the TYPE string for the printed "List type and amount:" space is hsa:/writableSchedule1Line8zOtherIncomeType, which EXISTS and is a single String shared by every computed leg this dictionary routes to line 8z. That is fgv finding FED-1099MISC-8Z-TYPESTRING-015, a real defect rather than an absence: a return with two 8z legs cannot describe either correctly, and this module now contributes THREE of them (box 3, box 8 and box 15). The per-entry shape income.xml uses for its own unemployment-adjacent 8z entries is the fix; hsa.xml was not granted to the unit that measured this.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 AND $0 ON EVERY COMMITTED SCENARIO. The Switch's first arm needs /form1099MiscOtherIncomeItems Complete; the default arm is a hard $0, so a return with no Form 1099-MISC at all, or one whose forms are all Alaska PFDs, contributes a hard zero to Schedule 1 line 9 without reading a money box.
EXCLUDES A PRIZE-CLASSIFIED ITEM (../isPrizeOrAward), so it does not double income:/prizesAwardsIncome (Schedule 1 line 8i) — the prize or award amount belongs on 8i only, and /form1099MiscPrizesAndAwards carries it there automatically. The application must not ask the filer to re-enter it on income:/writablePrizesAwards, which is scoped to prizes not reported on an entered Form 1099-MISC.
PHYSICAL-INJURY DAMAGES ARE LEFT OUT. The box 3 term sums /form1099MiscOtherIncomeItems/*/box3OtherIncomeForLine8z, which is box 3 less any part the filer identifies as compensatory damages for a personal physical injury or physical sickness (../writableBox3PhysicalInjuryDamages): Pub. 525 says not to include those in income, and the recipient instruction says to report correctly when a form cannot be corrected.
EXCLUDES A TRADE-OR-BUSINESS ITEM (../isTradeOrBusiness) as well. The same recipient instruction ends "If it is trade or business income, report this amount on Schedule C or F (Form 1040)", so the amount belongs on Schedule C line 1 (where it reaches self-employment tax, Schedule C expenses and the qualified business income deduction), not here. /form1099Miscs/*/tradeOrBusinessOtherIncome carries it into the Schedule C receipts floor, which the Schedule C line 1 reconciliation and /knockoutForm1099MiscScheduleCReceiptsWithoutScheduleC hold.

Fact.Name: Is Complete
Fact.Description:
Whether this Form 1099-MISC is complete: box 3 (../writableOtherIncome) answered, box 4 (../writableFederalWithholding) answered, box 8 (../writableSubstitutePayments) answered, box 15 (../writableNonqualifiedDeferredCompensation) answered, the Alaska PFD classification (../writableIsAlaskaPfd) answered, and the last available screen seen (../hasSeenLastAvailableScreen answered true). Each conjunct is an IsComplete test, so an abandoned item resolves Complete false rather than Placeholder.
Box 4 is required because it can hold backup withholding or withholding on Indian gaming distributions (IRC 3402(r)(1)), which IRC 31(a)(1) allows as a credit on Form 1040 line 25b; ../federalWithholding reads an unanswered box 4 as $0. The classification is required here, rather than by changing ../isAlaskaPfd's unanswered default, so every aggregate that reads ../isAlaskaPfd resolves as before and only this item's completeness reacts.
Box 8 and box 15 are required for the same reason as box 4: a blank box on a transcribed Form 1099-MISC cannot be told apart from an amount the filer has not yet entered. Box 8 substitute payments and box 15 nonqualified deferred compensation both reach Schedule 1 line 8z through their own complete-safe $0 wrappers (../substitutePaymentsForOtherIncome, ../nonqualifiedDeferredCompensationForOtherIncome), and box 15 also floors the section 409A additional tax at Schedule 2 line 17h (/form1099MiscSection409AAdditionalTaxFloor); leaving either box unanswered at its complete-safe $0 would drop that income, and the box 15 floor, without the filer ever having said so. The requirement is placed here, rather than by changing the two wrappers' unanswered defaults, so every total that reads them resolves as before and only this item's completeness reacts.
/primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Miscs and /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Miscs count items that are not complete and block submission until they are.

Fact.Name: At least one of Primary Filer's Form 1099-MISCs are incomplete
Fact.Description:
Whether at least one of the primary filer's Forms 1099-MISC is incomplete. When true, the return cannot be submitted.
Two independent counts. The first counts reports the primary filer owns (/form1099Miscs/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) whose /form1099Miscs/*/isComplete is false: box 3, box 4, box 8, box 15, the Alaska PFD classification or the last screen left unanswered. The second counts reports with no recipient assigned (/form1099Miscs/*/filer unanswered). It does not read the ownership alias, which resolves complete-safe false on an unassigned report, so an unassigned report still blocks and this guard resolves Complete true rather than Placeholder.
Why it blocks: /form1099Miscs/*/federalWithholding derives $0 on an unanswered box 4, and box 4 carries backup withholding or withholding on Indian gaming distributions that IRC 31(a)(1) allows as a Form 1040 line 25b credit. Without the block, a return holding an unfinished report files with that credit dropped. Box 8 and box 15 block for the same reason: ../substitutePaymentsForOtherIncome and ../nonqualifiedDeferredCompensationForOtherIncome both derive $0 on an unanswered box, and box 15 also floors the section 409A additional tax. This is the data-completeness guard formW2s, unemployment, socialSecurity and interest ship on their /primaryFilerHasIncomplete facts. The remedy is the filer finishing the report, so it is not a flow:/flowIsKnockedOut member and routes to no knockout screen.
Witnesses, Complete true: misc-abandoned-item-primary-refused, misc-unanswered-amount-primary-refused, misc-box4-blank-last-screen-seen-refused, misc-box8-blank-item-otherwise-complete-refused, misc-box15-blank-item-otherwise-complete-refused, misc-collection-one-complete-one-abandoned-refused, misc-answered-item-filer-unanswered-refused, misc-abandoned-item-filer-unanswered-refused (recipient never answered, blocked by the second count) and misc-mfj-item-filer-unanswered-both-refused. Complete false: misc-answered-item-no-refusal and misc-no-forms-complete-safe-false. The secondary filer's arm is /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Miscs.

Fact.Name: At least one of Secondary Filer's Form 1099-MISCs are incomplete
Fact.Description:
Whether at least one of the secondary filer's Forms 1099-MISC is incomplete. When true, the return cannot be submitted.
The secondary filer's arm of /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Miscs, over /form1099Miscs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler, with the same count of reports that have no recipient assigned, fenced to a joint return: that count fires here only when filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ is answered and true, so a return without a secondary filer is refused once, by the primary guard, and an unanswered filing status leaves this guard Complete false. Read that fact for why it blocks and why it is not a flow:/flowIsKnockedOut member.

Whether secondary filer has forms when primary filer is not filing jointly. It does not refuse a spouse's Form 1099-MISC whose box 3 Form 8958 line 12 gives this return half of. The third conjunct is Not(gate AND community), the interest.xml shape rather than a bare Not(gate), because box 3 is community income only when the filer says so: a spouse's SEPARATE box 3 on a non-joint return still has no line to sit on, and an UNANSWERED character is ../isCommunityIncome false, so silence keeps refusing rather than allocating. An Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend also keeps refusing, by the same conjunct — ../isCommunityIncome carries Not(../isAlaskaPfd) — and so does a spouse's item whose CLASSIFICATION is unanswered, because the legacy arm of ../isAlaskaPfd resolves an unanswered classification to TRUE.
THIS SHAPE IS SAFE ONLY BECAUSE /form1099MiscOtherIncome DOES NOT CARRY A SPOUSE'S COMMUNITY BOX 3 WHOLE: /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded (with its Form 1040 line 25b twin /communityPropertyOtherIncomeWithholdingAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, both below) subtracts the community half from the item total, so a return freed here files only the filer's own half.
WHICH GUARD HOLDS THE REST. filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws arm 2 refuses a community-property allocation return only while filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete is false, that is, until the all-community-income attestation, the lived-together answer and every owed per-item character question are answered. A return with every input answered is freed there.
A FOURTH POPULATION STAYS REFUSED: a spouse's item characterised as trade or business income (../isTradeOrBusiness). It leaves line 8z for the Schedule C receipts floor, which has no per-spouse split, and the line 8z allocation skips it, so the carve-out excludes it.
A SPOUSE'S COMMUNITY PRIZE IS NOT REFUSED BY THIS GUARD, like any other community box 3 item (filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws still decides whether the return files): /form1099MiscPrizesAndAwards (Schedule 1 line 8i) carries its own Form 8958 adjustment, /communityPropertyPrizeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, so a freed prize files only this return's half.
THE COMPLETENESS SHAPE. Two conjuncts sit at the top of the Derived All - IsComplete(filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ) and IsComplete(filers:/secondaryFiler) - because /form1099Miscs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler compares ../filer with filers:/secondaryFiler, and on a SINGLE-FILER return /secondaryFiler is a Find that resolves to nothing, so this guard, the collection guard's Count(...) > 0 and everything reading them would otherwise never resolve - the knockout could not be shown false and the return could not be proved clean. NO REFUSAL MOVES: All short-circuits on a Complete-false operand, so the only transition is Incomplete -> Complete false. LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE: an unanswered ../filer on a TWO-FILER non-MFJ return keeps the base's value byte-for-byte (Incomplete), because filers:/secondaryFiler is Complete there - which is why the conjunct is IsComplete(filers:/secondaryFiler) and not IsComplete(../belongsToSecondaryFiler) (../belongsToSecondaryFiler is itself IsComplete-first, so this conjunct is behaviourally a no-op there, kept for class uniformity).

Whether secondary filer has forms when primary filer is not filing jointly.
THE COLLECTION-LEVEL SIBLING. It is Count(the per-item guard) > 0, so it narrows exactly as the per-item guard narrows, with no edit of its own; the ANY quantifier is deliberate and still matches the harm, because one still-refused spouse item is enough to make the return unfilable no matter how many freed ones sit beside it.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Is the income on this Form 1099-MISC (boxes 3, 8 and 15) community income?
Fact.Description:
THE PER-ITEM CHARACTER INPUT for Form 8958 line 12. Line 12 is the form's RESIDUAL row — "Identify any item not previously reported, such as social security" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, RIGHT column of a two column extraction) — so it names no characterisation rule of its own, and the form puts the determination on the filer: "You and your spouse or RDP must be able to identify your" community and separate income (same file, line 147, LEFT column). Box 3 "Other income" is itself residual, so nothing in the document identifies the character either.
ONE ANSWER GOVERNS THREE BOXES. The same answer halves this document's box 3 (through ../isCommunityIncome, and only on an item that is not an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend or trade or business income), its box 8 substitute payments (../communityPropertyAllocatedSubstitutePaymentsUnrounded) and its box 15 nonqualified deferred compensation (../communityPropertyAllocatedNqdcUnrounded). The screen therefore asks about the income on the whole document, not box 3 alone. A document whose boxes differ in character (for example community box 3 and separate box 15) cannot be stated with one answer; that is a named residue, not handled here.
NO DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY. An unanswered character makes ../isCommunityIncome FALSE, which leaves the item UNALLOCATED and leaves ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ refusing when the item is the spouse's. Fail closed; this dictionary never assumes community.
IT MOVES A DOLLAR ONLY ON A NON-PFD ITEM: ../isAlaskaPfd is a per-item classification with a legacy-True unanswered arm, so an answered-true character on a non-PFD item makes ../isCommunityIncome TRUE and the allocated half real. The half reaches Schedule 1 line 8z through /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, the box 4 half reaches Form 1040 line 25b through its twin, and ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ narrows with them, so an answer of TRUE here on a spouse's non-PFD item can be the difference between a refused return and a filable one, once filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete is also satisfied (see ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ for which populations still refuse).

Fact.Name: This payer's box 3 other income is community income
Fact.Description:
../writableIsCommunityIncome read complete safe, AND NOT an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend. IsComplete FIRST, so an unanswered character resolves FALSE rather than Incomplete.
THE ALASKA CONJUNCT DECIDES EVERY PFD CASE. ../isAlaskaPfd is a per-item classification with a legacy-True unanswered arm, so this fact is FALSE whenever the item is (or, unanswered, defaults to) an Alaska PFD, no matter what the filer attests to the community character; on an item answered not-a-PFD this fact follows the filer's character attestation. That is the contract's own carve-out made mechanical: an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend is not community income of a couple domiciled in a community property state, and /alaskaPfdIncome — the ONLY chain by which box 3 reaches a Form 1040 line — must never be reached by the allocation.
FAIL CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: an unanswered character does not allocate, and an ATTESTED community character does not allocate an APFD either.

Fact.Name: This payer's community-property character question is unanswered
Fact.Description:
TRUE while the per-item character question has no answer on an item whose answer can matter, FALSE the moment the filer answers it either way.
AN ALASKA PERMANENT FUND DIVIDEND WITH NOTHING IN BOX 8 OR BOX 15 IS NOT ASKED. ../isCommunityIncome carries Not(../isAlaskaPfd), so the box 3 half of a PFD item is never allocated whatever the character answer is. Demanding that inert answer would keep a community-property return refused over a question that cannot move a dollar. But box 8 and box 15 are allocated on the character answer itself (../communityPropertyAllocatedSubstitutePaymentsUnrounded, ../communityPropertyAllocatedNqdcUnrounded), not on ../isCommunityIncome, so on a PFD item that carries a box 8 or box 15 amount the answer does move a dollar and is still owed. An item whose PFD classification is itself unanswered takes ../isAlaskaPfd's legacy TRUE arm, so it is counted here only when it carries a box 8 or box 15 amount; either way it is already an incomplete report (../isComplete requires the classification), so no return files on that silence. WHY IT EXISTS: filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete may lift the arm of filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws that reads the allocation gate only on a return whose EVERY present item is characterised, so an unanswered character must be VISIBLE at the return level rather than silently defaulted. This fact changes no figure: an unanswered character still allocates nothing (../isCommunityIncome stays false) exactly as before. Read only by /form1099Miscs/communityPropertyCharacterisationIncomplete.

Fact.Name: Some Form 1099-MISC community-property character is unanswered
Fact.Description: GreaterThan(Count of per-item unanswered characters, 0), the same return-level shape as /form1099Miscs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ. Read by filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete, whose IsComplete-first wrapper is what keeps filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws complete-safe when this collection is absent: an absent root is Placeholder on the JVM, the wrapper reads that as NOT complete, and the refusal stands. Fail closed.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 12 column B/C — this return's half of this payer's box 3
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE Form 1099-MISC's box 3 other income (the part that reaches line 8z, ../box3OtherIncomeForLine8z, so excluded physical-injury damages are not halved), on a return that must allocate community income AND on an item the filer has characterised as community income that is not an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend. $0 on every other item and on every other return, by ../isCommunityIncome's Alaska conjunct; a non-PFD item answered community is a real half.
THE HALF IS THE FORM'S OPERATIVE SENTENCE, not a line 12 rule: "You must report half of all community income and all of your" separate income (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, LEFT column). Line 12 itself says only to allocate, with no ratio.
A TRADE-OR-BUSINESS ITEM (../isTradeOrBusiness) ALLOCATES NOTHING HERE: the amount halved is ../box3OtherIncomeForCommunityAllocation, which is $0 on such an item, because its box 3 leaves line 8z for Schedule C line 1 (../tradeOrBusinessOtherIncome) and a Schedule C carries its own Form 8958 split, so halving it here as well would take the half off twice.
NOT ROUNDED TO THE DOLLAR: shaped as the addend it is. Box 3 reaches a Form 1040 line through Schedule 1 line 8z, via /form1099MiscOtherIncome: the adjustment fact /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded is MINUS the CollectionSum of these halves, and it enters /form1099MiscOtherIncome inside that fact's Round, so line 8z rounds once, over this addend's cents.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-MISC's box 3 amount that the line 8z Form 8958 allocation halves
Fact.Description: ../box3OtherIncomeForLine8z, or $0 when the filer identified box 3 as trade or business income (../isTradeOrBusiness) or as a prize or award (../isPrizeOrAward). Read only by ../communityPropertyAllocatedOtherIncomeUnrounded. A trade-or-business item's box 3 leaves line 8z for Schedule C line 1, and the Schedule C carries its own Form 8958 split, so the line 8z allocation must not halve it a second time. A prize item's box 3 is on line 8i, and its half is taken off line 8i by /communityPropertyPrizeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, not off line 8z. An H-2A compensation item's box 3 is wages on Form 1040 line 1h, and an allocating return that carries it is refused by filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete until its split is built. Every other item passes ../box3OtherIncomeForLine8z through unchanged, Incomplete included, so a blank box 3 or an exclusion above box 3 still fails closed.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 12 — the half of this payer's box 3 prize or award that goes to the other spouse
Fact.Description: Half of ONE Form 1099-MISC's box 3 when the filer identified it as a prize or award (../isPrizeOrAward), on a return that must allocate community income (filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn) and an item answered community income (../isCommunityIncome, which already excludes an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend); $0 on every other item and return. Cents kept: /communityPropertyPrizeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded negates the sum and /form1099MiscPrizesAndAwards adds it, so line 8i carries the filer's own half of a community prize (whole minus half of the filer's item; the spouse's item, freed by ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ, likewise contributes whole minus half).

Fact.Name: Form 8958 adjustment to the Form 1099-MISC prize leg of Schedule 1 line 8i, unrounded
Fact.Description: MINUS the sum of ../communityPropertyAllocatedPrizeUnrounded over the collection: a negative, cents-bearing addend of /form1099MiscPrizesAndAwards, so line 8i carries this return's half of every community prize and rounds once in income:/prizesAwardsIncome. $0 on every return the allocation gate reads false on, and $0 over an empty or unopened collection.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated Form 1099-MISC box 3 and prize halves (disclosure total)
Fact.Description:
The whole-dollar total of the community halves of Form 1099-MISC box 3 other income and of box 3 prizes and awards, over every payer whose amount is community income: the per payer halves are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once here. It is $0 when no non-Alaska-PFD item is answered community, because /form1099Miscs/*/isCommunityIncome carries a Not(../isAlaskaPfd) conjunct.
IT IS NOT A PRINTED FIGURE. The Form 8958 line 12 Form 1099-MISC row is composed in the form8958 module (form8958:/form8958Line12OtherIncomeColumnCSpouseShare and its column B and A siblings) from the two Schedule 1 adjustments, which also carry the box 8 and box 15 halves this total leaves out, so this total is smaller than that column whenever a community box 8 or box 15 amount is present. It is not the adjustment either: Schedule 1 lines 8z and 8i move through the unrounded, negated /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded and /communityPropertyPrizeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded. No fact reads this total; it is exported and kept as the checked box 3 disclosure figure that the node tests pin.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 12 column B/C — this return's half of this payer's box 8
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE Form 1099-MISC's box 8 substitute payments, before rounding. It is half of the complete-safe ../substitutePaymentsForOtherIncome amount only when this return must allocate community income and the filer answered this document's community character TRUE; it is $0 otherwise. Box 8 has its own Schedule 1 line 8z route, so this half is included in the same line 8z adjustment as box 3 and remains separate from the Form 8958 disclosure total for box 3.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated 1099-MISC box 8 substitute payments, unrounded
Fact.Description: The unrounded sum of this return's per-payer community halves of Form 1099-MISC box 8 substitute payments. It is used only by /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, where it joins the box 3 half as a negative addend inside the single Schedule 1 line 8z Round.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 12 column B/C, this return's half of this payer's box 15
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE Form 1099-MISC's box 15 nonqualified deferred compensation, before rounding. It is half of the complete-safe ../nonqualifiedDeferredCompensationForOtherIncome amount only when this return must allocate community income AND the filer answered this document's community character TRUE; it is $0 otherwise. Box 15 has its own Schedule 1 line 8z route, so this half joins the box 3 and box 8 halves in the same line 8z adjustment. The explicit writable character is read rather than ../isCommunityIncome for box 8's reason: a box 15 amount stays allocable on a document whose separate box 3 is an Alaska PFD.
THE FLOOR IS BUILT ON THE SAME HALF: the filer enters the line matching the income they reported, which is exactly why the floor must be measured against that same income. A floor on the un-halved total would compare a whole bound against a halved entry and refuse the correct return: 20 percent of 500.00 is 100.00, the lawful line 17h on the 350.00 this return includes is 70.00. The floor reads /form1099MiscIncludibleNqdcTotal, which is the box 15 total MINUS this very sum, so the tax and its own income leg are allocated identically and neither can drift from the other.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated 1099-MISC box 15 nonqualified deferred compensation, unrounded
Fact.Description: The unrounded sum of this return's per-payer community halves of Form 1099-MISC box 15. It is used only by /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, where it joins the box 3 and box 8 halves as a negative addend inside the single Schedule 1 line 8z Round.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 11 column B/C — this return's half of this payer's box 4
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE Form 1099-MISC's box 4 federal income tax withheld, on a return that must allocate community income AND on an item the filer has characterised as community income that is not an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend. $0 on every other item and on every other return.
IT MOVES ON EXACTLY THE SAME ITEMS AND THE SAME HALVES as ../communityPropertyAllocatedOtherIncomeUnrounded, because the credit follows the income it was withheld from: "each of you is entitled to credit for half the income tax withheld on" community income (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4). Withholding on a SEPARATE property item is entirely its owner's credit and is not halved, which is why this switches on ../isCommunityIncome rather than on the gate alone.
NOT ROUNDED TO THE DOLLAR: Form 1040 line 25b rounds once, at /form1099MiscFederalIncomeTaxWithheld, over cents-bearing addends.
THE HALF IS CENT-SCALED AND HALF-EVEN, exactly as on the wages and interest twins — Multiply(Rational 1/2, Dollar) does not carry a half cent — so on an odd-cent box 4 the two spouses' halves can total one cent away from column A, against the form's own "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction). Nothing in this dictionary can remove that; it is disclosed rather than hidden.
The gate filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is complete-safe false, so an unanswered domicile leaves this Complete at $0 rather than Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated 1099-MISC withholding (Form 8958 line 11)
Fact.Description:
The column B/C figure of Form 8958 line 11 for Form 1099-MISC box 4, totalled over every payer whose box 3 is community income. Whole dollars — the per-payer halves are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once here.
THE DISCLOSURE FIGURE, not the adjustment. The number Form 1040 line 25b actually carries moves through /communityPropertyOtherIncomeWithholdingAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, which is an addend of /form1099MiscFederalIncomeTaxWithheld. Line 11 of Form 8958 is one printed row for the whole return, so this fact is this module's contribution to it beside formW2s:/communityPropertyAllocatedFederalWithholding and interest:/communityPropertyAllocatedInterestTaxWithheld.
$0 on every return the allocation gate reads false on, and $0 on every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: The community box 3, box 8 and box 15 halves that leave this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description:
A NEGATIVE, cents-bearing addend of Schedule 1 line 8z: MINUS the sum of the per-payer community halves of Form 1099-MISC box 3, box 8 and box 15. Box 8 and box 15 use their own explicit community character and are included even when the same document's box 3 is an Alaska PFD. Box 15 has its own line 8z route; it would otherwise be the one line 8z addend allocated at 100 percent on a community-property return.
WHY THE NEGATION AND NOT THE WAGES UNIT'S allocated-MINUS-unscoped, in one line: this collection is MIXED, so the wages formula would delete the filer's OWN separate box 3 and the filer's OWN Alaska PFD from the line. The full argument, with interest.xml's worked $1,000/$300 arithmetic, is in the block comment above this fact.
WHY AN ADDEND AND NOT A REPLACEMENT, and why ONE addend is enough here where the wages unit needed its addend in two chains: Schedule 1 line 8z is printed by hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome and totalled into line 9 by income:/otherIncome, and BOTH of them read the single fact /form1099MiscOtherIncome. Entering that fact once therefore moves the printed box and the total together, and they cannot disagree about the allocation. This footing discipline is satisfied by construction rather than by a second addend.
NO GATE ON THIS FACT, deliberately, matching interest.xml: every addend of the CollectionSum is already $0 whenever filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is false, so this fact is $0 there too, with one fewer gate read in front of a printed line. That gate is complete-safe FALSE, so an unanswered domicile changes nothing.
WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH. /alaskaPfdIncome (Schedule 1 line 8g) is untouched, because every addend carries ../isCommunityIncome and that fact's Not(../isAlaskaPfd) conjunct makes an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend contribute $0. The allocation reaching line 8g is what the records contract forbade and it still cannot happen.
A BOUNDED ROUNDING RESIDUE, disclosed: this addend is cents-bearing and enters /form1099MiscOtherIncome INSIDE its Round, so line 8z rounds once over the whole sum. The disclosure total /communityPropertyAllocatedOtherIncome rounds the same halves separately, so the two can differ by under a dollar; a second, rounded basis was considered and rejected for the reason interest.xml gives — it would put two different allocation figures in the dictionary for one Form 8958 line.

Fact.Name: The community box 4 half that leaves this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description:
The Form 1040 line 25b twin of /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded: a NEGATIVE, cents-bearing addend equal to MINUS the sum of the per-payer box 4 halves. Same shape and same reasoning — the negation, not the wages unit's allocated-minus-unscoped, because withholding on a SEPARATE property item, and on an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend, is entirely its owner's credit and must not be halved.
IT IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT IS WHY THIS UNIT IS FOUR FACTS RATHER THAN TWO. /form1099MiscFederalIncomeTaxWithheld sums the collection with NO filer filter, so the guard narrowing in this unit would otherwise let a freed spouse-owned community Form 1099-MISC put the WHOLE of the spouse's box 4 on this return's line 25b while line 8z carried only half its box 3 — an overstated credit, and internally inconsistent besides. The interest unit shipped its withholding twin on the same reasoning.
$0 on every return the gate reads false on, because every addend of the sum is. No gate of its own, for the same reason as the income twin.
PLACEMENT: this shape is the 3-of-5 MAJORITY. dividendReports and form1099Rs both net their allocation inside their own module total, the 1099-R comment verbatim: "netted here rather than at Form 1040 line 25b". Only interest and unemployment use the sibling-addend shape. This one is an addend of /form1099MiscFederalIncomeTaxWithheld itself, following the dividendReports/form1099Rs majority; inside this module's Round the whole quantity rounds exactly once, over cents, which is what i1040gi page 23 asks for. taxCalculations' line 25b Add carries three deliberately cents-bearing legs, as its own Description narrates. NOTHING ELSE READS THAT TOTAL: taxCalculations.xml's line 25b Add is its only reader, and it carries no mef export, so moving the allocation inside it changes nothing but line 25b. The per-document image /form1099Miscs/*/federalWithholding is UNCHANGED — an allocation is a return-level reporting rule, not a restatement of what the payer withheld, exactly as the unemployment unit says.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Did you receive a Form 1099-MISC?
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Did you receive a Form 1099-MISC for 2025?" Help text: A Form 1099-MISC reports miscellaneous income such as an Alaska Permanent Fund dividend, rents, royalties, prizes and awards, or other income of $600 or more — check every 1099-MISC you received, not only ones from Alaska. If unsure, look for a document titled "Form 1099-MISC" from a payer. Asked when: every filer, unconditionally — there is no gating fact and no residence test; the prior gate asked this only of Alaska residents. Unanswered posture: REFUSED. Leaving this unanswered leaves /isApfSectionComplete Complete FALSE, which blocks submission — deliberately, because the fact it replaces resolved every non-Alaska filer's section complete without asking anything, which is the defect. Validation: Boolean, no default. What the answer feeds: answering NO resolves /isApfSectionComplete Complete TRUE (Case 1) with no further screens owed; answering YES routes the filer into the /form1099Miscs item-adding screens that end in ../hasCompletedApfSection, Case 2 of the same fact, unchanged by this unit. Neither answer computes a dollar by itself — only the /form1099Miscs items entered under a YES do.
Whether the tax return has at least one completed APF income
The user has clicked "Done" for the APF section.

Whether the Form 1099-MISC section is complete: either the filer has answered "No" to /hasReceivedForm1099Misc (nothing to collect), or the filer has finished the section (../hasCompletedApfSection). Neither answer alone is enough on its own to leave the other unanswered.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC calendar year
Fact.Description: The "For calendar year" entry printed in the form's title block, as a four-digit year. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Calendar year shown on this Form 1099-MISC" (four digits), on the payer-identity screen, on every Form 1099-MISC item; never required. Help text: the year the payer printed after "For calendar year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099msc--2025.pdf, page 2); a form for a year other than 2025 belongs on that year's return or is a corrected prior-year form. Validation: exactly four digits. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-MISC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC VOID box
Fact.Description: The VOID checkbox in the form's header. It prints on Copy A and Copy 1 only (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099msc--2025.pdf, pages 2-3); the recipient's Copy B and Copy 2 do not carry it. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the VOID box checked on this Form 1099-MISC?" (yes/no), on every Form 1099-MISC item; never required. Help text: a payer checks VOID only on a Copy A it did not mean to file, so the IRS scanner skips it; a correction is never marked VOID (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099mec--2025.pdf, page 1, RIGHT column). Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-MISC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC CORRECTED box
Fact.Description: The CORRECTED checkbox in the form's header: "CORRECTED" on Copy A and Copy 1, "CORRECTED (if checked)" on the recipient's Copy B and Copy 2 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099msc--2025.pdf, pages 2, 3, 4, 6). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is this a CORRECTED Form 1099-MISC?" (yes/no), on every Form 1099-MISC item; never required. Help text: a payer who fixes a form it already filed sends a new one with CORRECTED checked; enter the corrected amounts, not the original ones (recipient instructions, "Form 1099-MISC incorrect?", same file lines 139-141, LEFT column). Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-MISC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC payer address and telephone
Fact.Description: The rest of the payer block after the payer's name: street address, city or town, state or province, country, ZIP or foreign postal code, and telephone number, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099msc--2025.pdf, page 2). The name itself is ../payer. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Payer's address and phone number" (free text, as printed), beside the payer's name, on every Form 1099-MISC item; never required. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; ../isComplete does not read it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns. Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC: this document's Schedule C receipts are already reported correctly
Fact.Description:

(yes/no), on a Form 1099-MISC item that carries a box 5, 6, 10 or 11 amount or a box 3 amount identified as trade or business income, and the application should raise it when scheduleC:/scheduleC1099MiscReceiptsConsistent would otherwise refuse; never required. IT READS /form1099MiscScheduleCReceiptsFenceFloor, not the raw total, so the IRS's own escape applies here exactly as it does to the Schedule C line 1 reconciliation: a document the filer attests is already reported correctly (the form is wrong or issued in error, or the income is reported elsewhere) is excused, per document.

Fact.Name: A Form 1099-MISC box 13 FATCA filing requirement is checked and the return is above the Form 8938 threshold, or that threshold is unanswered
Fact.Description:

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 15 nonqualified deferred compensation
Fact.Description: Form 1099-MISC box 15, Nonqualified deferred compensation (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099msc--2025.pdf, page 2). Validation: Dollar, Min $0. UNANSWERED: ../isComplete reads it — a blank box on a transcribed form is unknown, not a payer-reported $0 (box 4's reading) — so an unanswered box leaves the item incomplete and /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Miscs (or the secondary arm) holds the return; the complete-safe ../nonqualifiedDeferredCompensationForOtherIncome wrapper below still reads $0, so no total or the section 409A floor goes Incomplete on its account. Fact.Description: Complete-safe sum of the box 15 amounts across the collection, cents preserved. An unopened or empty collection contributes $0. Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 15 required to be included in THIS return's gross income
Fact.Description:
The box 15 total MINUS the Form 8958 halves this return allocates away: /form1099MiscNonqualifiedDeferredCompensationTotal less /communityPropertyAllocatedNqdcUnrounded. On every return that is not a community-property allocation return the subtrahend is a hard $0 and this fact equals the total.
THIS FACT IS THE BASE /form1099MiscSection409AAdditionalTaxFloor USES, NOT THE WHOLE BOX 15 TOTAL: IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(i)(II) prices the flat term at 20 percent of "the compensation which is required to be included in gross income", and on a Form 8958 return the spouse's half is required to be included in the SPOUSE'S gross income, not in this one. A floor built on the un-halved base would either overstate the filer's tax by 20 percent of the spouse's half or, when the filer enters the lawful figure, refuse a correct return outright.
THE SAME HALF THE INCOME LEG USES, by construction: this subtrahend is the identical fact /communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded negates into Schedule 1 line 8z, so the base of the tax and the income it is a tax on can never disagree about which dollars this return reports.
UNDER-BOUNDING IS THE SAFE DIRECTION and this fact only ever moves the floor DOWN. A smaller floor lets a return file that the statute might tax more heavily; a larger floor blocks a correct return from filing at all. Only the second is a defect.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0: the membership test is on the collection itself, never on an item, so an unopened /form1099Miscs contributes $0 rather than a Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 15: the section 409A premium interest on this amount
Fact.Description:
The interest component of the section 409A additional tax on THIS Form 1099-MISC's box 15 amount. AN ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION: IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(ii) prices it "at the underpayment rate plus 1 percentage point on the underpayments that would have occurred had the deferred compensation been includible in gross income for the taxable year in which first deferred or, if later, the first taxable year in which such deferred compensation is not subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture". Neither the year first deferred nor the rate history is carried by any box on this form or any fact in this dictionary, so the figure is the filer's own.
SCREEN SPEC: ask "Section 409A premium interest on this amount" (dollar amount), on a Form 1099-MISC item whose box 15 was answered with an amount above zero; never required. Help text: the interest part of the extra tax on income from a plan that failed section 409A, figured at the IRS underpayment rate plus one percentage point from the year the pay was first deferred. Validation: Dollar, Min $0. UNANSWERED: complete-safe $0 -- the 20 percent term alone is still a valid lower bound on the printed line, so leaving this blank weakens the floor rather than breaking the return.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../section409APremiumInterest and so /form1099MiscSection409AAdditionalTaxFloor. It is NOT itself a printed line: Schedule 2 line 17h remains the filer's own entry, and this figure only raises the floor that entry must clear.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-MISC box 15 premium interest, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Complete-safe reading of ../writableSection409APremiumInterest: the attested interest when the filer answered it, otherwise $0. An unanswered attestation lowers the floor to the flat 20 percent term, which is still a term the statute always adds.

Fact.Name: Total attested section 409A premium interest on this return's Forms 1099-MISC
Fact.Description: The sum, over every Form 1099-MISC, of the attested section 409A premium interest that goes with a box 15 amount, cents preserved and not rounded: the interest term of the section 409A additional tax. $0 when no Form 1099-MISC was entered or no interest was attested. Unrounded because Schedule 2 line 17h is a total that rounds once, after the 20 percent term and this interest are added (schedule2 /schedule2Line17hCombinedSection409AFloor reads it for that reason).

Fact.Name: The section 409A additional tax Form 1099-MISC box 15 alone establishes
Fact.Description:
The statutory LOWER BOUND on Schedule 2 line 17h that this return's Forms 1099-MISC establish on their own: Round(20 percent of the cents-preserving INCLUDIBLE box 15 total, /form1099MiscIncludibleNqdcTotal), plus the attested premium interest. It is the Form 1099-MISC figure alone: the bound the printed line must actually clear is schedule2 /schedule2Line17hCombinedSection409AFloor, which takes 20 percent of this box 15 base PLUS the Form W-2 box 12 code Z base and rounds once, because the same printed line carries both sources. The interest term is /form1099MiscSection409APremiumInterestTotal.
THE BASE IS THE INCLUDIBLE AMOUNT, NOT THE PRINTED TOTAL: on a Form 8958 return the spouse's half of a community box 15 amount is required to be included in the spouse's gross income, and the 20 percent term is priced on "the compensation which is required to be included in gross income". See /form1099MiscIncludibleNqdcTotal.
WHY A FLOOR AND NOT THE LINE. IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(i) makes the tax the SUM of two terms. The 20 percent term has no input this collection does not already hold, so it is computable and can never be zero while a positive box 15 exists. The interest term depends on the year the compensation was first deferred and on the underpayment rate in each year since, neither of which is on this form, so it enters only as far as the filer attested it. A line 17h entry BELOW this sum is therefore never "a smaller correct tax": it is an unanswered question or an entry that omits the flat term the statute always adds.
ONE Round, ON THE WHOLE BOUND. /form1099MiscNonqualifiedDeferredCompensationTotal preserves cents, the 20 percent term keeps its cents, the attested interest is added with its cents, and only the total rounds: the 1040 instructions say "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total", and Schedule 2 line 17h has no cents column. A cents-bearing bound compared against a filer who correctly rounded line 17h would refuse a correct return (a 2,350.25 bound against a 2,350 entry), which is why the bound is whole dollars.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0: both terms are complete-safe, so this fact is a hard $0 on every return with no box 15 amount, which is every committed scenario at this HEAD.
